#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate Fig 2: ISR collapse trajectory — ISR reward causes tautological collapse."""

import json
import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ── Okabe-Ito palette (colorblind-safe, consistent with other figures) ──
OI_BLUE = "#0072B2"
OI_RED  = "#D55E00"
OI_SKY  = "#56B4E9"

# ── Style ──
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 11,
    "axes.titlesize": 13, "axes.labelsize": 12,
    "xtick.labelsize": 10, "ytick.labelsize": 10,
    "legend.fontsize": 10, "figure.dpi": 300,
    "savefig.dpi": 300, "savefig.bbox": "tight",
    "savefig.pad_inches": 0.05,
    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "lines.linewidth": 1.8, "pdf.fonttype": 42, "ps.fonttype": 42,
})


def rolling_mean(arr, w=20):
    kernel = np.ones(w) / w
    padded = np.concatenate([np.full(w - 1, arr[0]), arr])
    return np.convolve(padded, kernel, mode="valid")


# ── Load data ──
data_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "fig2_data.json")
with open(data_path) as f:
    data = json.load(f)

W = 20

exec_s44_steps = np.array(data["exec_s44"]["steps"])
exec_s44_smooth = rolling_mean(np.array(data["exec_s44"]["isr"]), W)

isr_s44_steps = np.array(data["isr_s44"]["steps"])
isr_s44_smooth = rolling_mean(np.array(data["isr_s44"]["isr"]), W)

isr_1k_steps = np.array(data["isr_s42_1000"]["steps"])
isr_1k_smooth = rolling_mean(np.array(data["isr_s42_1000"]["isr"]), W)

rand_s44_steps = np.array(data["random_s44"]["steps"])
rand_s44_smooth = rolling_mean(np.array(data["random_s44"]["isr"]), W)

# ── Plot ──
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))

# ISR β=0.1: two seeds showing collapse
ax.plot(isr_s44_steps, isr_s44_smooth, color=OI_RED, linewidth=2.2,
        label=r"ISR $\beta\!=\!0.1$ (seed 44)", zorder=5)
ax.plot(isr_1k_steps, isr_1k_smooth, color=OI_RED, linewidth=1.2,
        alpha=0.5, linestyle="--",
        label=r"ISR $\beta\!=\!0.1$ (seed 42, 1k steps)", zorder=4)

# Exec-only
ax.plot(exec_s44_steps, exec_s44_smooth, color=OI_BLUE, linewidth=2.2,
        label="Exec-only (seed 44)", zorder=5)

# Random β=0.1
ax.plot(rand_s44_steps, rand_s44_smooth, color=OI_SKY, linewidth=2.2,
        label=r"Random $\beta\!=\!0.1$ (seed 44)", zorder=5)

# Annotation: ISR collapse
collapse_step = 280
collapse_isr = isr_s44_smooth[collapse_step - 1]
ax.annotate("ISR collapse\n(Goodhart effect)",
            xy=(collapse_step, collapse_isr),
            xytext=(100, 0.92),
            fontsize=9, color=OI_RED, fontweight="bold",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=OI_RED, lw=1.2),
            ha="center", va="center")

ax.set_xlabel("Training Step")
ax.set_ylabel("ISR (proved samples only, rolling $w$=20)")
ax.set_ylim(-0.02, 1.02)
ax.set_xlim(0, 1050)
ax.legend(loc="center right", framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="none")
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linewidth=0.5)

# ── Save ──
out_dir = os.path.dirname(__file__)
for ext in ("pdf", "png"):
    out = os.path.join(out_dir, f"fig2_isr_collapse.{ext}")
    fig.savefig(out, format=ext)
    print(f"Saved: {out}")
plt.close()

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({'pdf.fonttype': 42, 'ps.fonttype': 42,
                     'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans', 'font.size': 9,
                     'axes.labelsize': 9, 'axes.titlesize': 10,
                     'xtick.labelsize': 9, 'ytick.labelsize': 9})

C_FOL = '#0072B2'
C_PROLOG = '#56B4E9'
C_TS = '#D55E00'

seeds = ['s42', 's43', 's44']

bar_w = 0.32

fol_isr = [0.132, 0.000, 0.582]
prolog_isr = [0.037, 0.015, 0.387]
fol_pr = [93, 14, 98]
prolog_pr = [83, 56, 21]

h7 = [100, 0, 0]
degen = [0, 100, 0]
query = [0, 0, 100]

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(3.25, 4.8),
                                gridspec_kw={'hspace': 0.55})

# === Top Panel ===
b1 = ax1.bar(x - bar_w/2, fol_isr, bar_w, color=C_FOL, label='FOL', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)
b2 = ax1.bar(x + bar_w/2, prolog_isr, bar_w, color=C_PROLOG, label='Prolog', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

# PR labels — per-seed (fol_y_offset, prolog_y_offset, fol_ha, prolog_ha, fol_x_off, prolog_x_off)
pr_cfg = [
    (0.02, 0.02, 'center', 'left',   0,    0.04),  # s42: PR=83% shift right
    (0.10, 0.02, 'center', 'left',   0,    0),      # s43: PR=14%† centered
    (0.02, 0.02, 'center', 'left',   0,    0.04),  # s44: PR=21% shift right + line break
]
PR_FS = 6

for i, (bar, pr) in enumerate(zip(b1, fol_pr)):
    label = f'PR={pr}%'
    if i == 1:
        label += '†'
    bx = bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2 + pr_cfg[i][4]
    by = bar.get_height() + pr_cfg[i][0]
    ax1.text(bx, by, label, ha=pr_cfg[i][2], va='bottom', fontsize=PR_FS, color=C_FOL)

for i, (bar, pr) in enumerate(zip(b2, prolog_pr)):
    label = f'PR={pr}%'
    if i == 2:
        label = f'PR={pr}%\n($n$=21)'
    bx = bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2 + pr_cfg[i][5]
    by = bar.get_height() + pr_cfg[i][1]
    ax1.text(bx, by, label, ha=pr_cfg[i][3], va='bottom', fontsize=PR_FS, color='#3a7abf')

ax1.set_xticks(x)
ax1.set_xticklabels(seeds)
ax1.set_ylabel('ISR* (exec-only)')
ax1.set_ylim(0, 0.78)
ax1.set_yticks(np.arange(0, 0.8, 0.1))
ax1.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper left', frameon=False)
ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax1.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax1.set_title('(a) Exec-only ISR*: FOL vs Prolog', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', loc='left', pad=4)

# footnote moved to LaTeX caption for readability

# === Bottom Panel ===
bw2 = bar_w * 1.6
b_h7 = ax2.bar(x, h7, bw2, color=C_TS, label='TS tautological', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)
b_degen = ax2.bar(x, degen, bw2, bottom=h7, color=C_DEGEN, label='Degenerate syntax', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)
b_query = ax2.bar(x, query, bw2, bottom=[h+d for h,d in zip(h7, degen)], color=C_QUERY, label='Query-as-fact', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

ax2.set_xticks(x)
ax2.set_xticklabels(seeds)
ax2.set_ylabel('Percentage (%)')
ax2.set_ylim(0, 120)
ax2.set_yticks([0, 25, 50, 75, 100])
ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax2.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax2.set_title('(b) Prolog STA Gaming Modes', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', loc='left', pad=4)

ax2.text(1.0, 108, '3/3 seeds gaming, 0% genuine', ha='center',
         fontsize=8, fontstyle='italic', color=C_TS)

ax2.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper center', frameon=False, ncol=3,
           bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.15), columnspacing=0.6, handletextpad=0.3)

mode_labels = ['TS\ntautol.', 'Degen.\nsyntax', 'Query-\nas-fact']
colors_text = ['white', 'black', 'white']
for i, (lbl, ct) in enumerate(zip(mode_labels, colors_text)):
    ax2.text(x[i], 50, lbl, ha='center', va='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold', color=ct)

out_pdf = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_3/projects/solver-trace-ablation/docs/paper/figures/fig4_prolog_comparison.pdf'

print(f'Saved: {out_png}')

     \begin{abstract}
     We study structural degeneration in neurosymbolic reasoning trained with GRPO: models achieve high prove rates while most outputs embed the conclusion among premises---a degenerate shortcut invisible to execution reward.
     We introduce \emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA), a diagnostic applying leave-one-out necessity testing to solver inputs; the fraction of necessary components yields the \emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR), whose diagnostic value is realized through mode-level analysis.
     As a diagnostic, component-necessity testing reveals a collapse trajectory hidden from prove rate: the mode breakdown shows dominant structural hacking while prove rate rises, with each seed converging to a qualitatively different hacking mode; a supervised fine-tuning baseline corroborates that the degradation is GRPO-specific.
     When repurposed as a training reward, ISR exhibits a seed-dependent regressional Goodhart effect: hacking composition shifts from conclusion embedding to tautological shortcutting without reducing overall prevalence, though the effect is stochastic---some seeds retain substantial genuine reasoning.
     Cross-logic and cross-dataset evidence confirms structural degeneration generalizes, documenting ISR's core asymmetry: reliable as a diagnostic, dataset-dependent as an optimization target.\footnote{Code and data: \url{[anonymized]}}

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

plt.rcParams.update({'pdf.fonttype': 42, 'ps.fonttype': 42,
                     'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans', 'font.size': 9,
                     'axes.labelsize': 9, 'axes.titlesize': 10,
                     'xtick.labelsize': 9, 'ytick.labelsize': 9})

C_FOL = '#0072B2'
C_PROLOG = '#56B4E9'
C_TS = '#D55E00'
C_DEGEN = '#E69F00'
C_QUERY = '#CC79A7'

seeds = ['s42', 's43', 's44']
x = np.arange(len(seeds))
bar_w = 0.32

fol_isr = [0.132, 0.000, 0.582]
prolog_isr = [0.037, 0.015, 0.387]
fol_pr = [93, 14, 98]
prolog_pr = [83, 56, 21]

h7 = [100, 0, 0]
degen = [0, 100, 0]
query = [0, 0, 100]

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(3.25, 4.8),
                                gridspec_kw={'hspace': 0.55})

# === Top Panel ===
b1 = ax1.bar(x - bar_w/2, fol_isr, bar_w, color=C_FOL, label='FOL', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)
b2 = ax1.bar(x + bar_w/2, prolog_isr, bar_w, color=C_PROLOG, label='Prolog', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

# PR labels — per-seed (fol_y_offset, prolog_y_offset, fol_ha, prolog_ha, fol_x_off, prolog_x_off)
pr_cfg = [
    (0.02, 0.02, 'center', 'right', 0,    0.02),  # s42: right-align to bar right edge
    (0.10, 0.02, 'center', 'right', 0,    0.02),  # s43: right-align to bar right edge
    (0.02, 0.02, 'center', 'right', 0,    0.02),  # s44: right-align to bar right edge
]
PR_FS = 6

for i, (bar, pr) in enumerate(zip(b1, fol_pr)):
    label = f'PR={pr}%'
    if i == 1:
        label += '†'
    bx = bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2 + pr_cfg[i][4]
    by = bar.get_height() + pr_cfg[i][0]
    ax1.text(bx, by, label, ha=pr_cfg[i][2], va='bottom', fontsize=PR_FS, color=C_FOL)

for i, (bar, pr) in enumerate(zip(b2, prolog_pr)):
    label = f'PR={pr}%'
    if i == 2:
        label = f'PR={pr}%\n($n$=21)'
    bx = bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2 + pr_cfg[i][5]
    by = bar.get_height() + pr_cfg[i][1]
    ax1.text(bx, by, label, ha=pr_cfg[i][3], va='bottom', fontsize=PR_FS, color='#3a7abf')

ax1.set_xticks(x)
ax1.set_xticklabels(seeds)
ax1.set_ylabel('ISR* (exec-only)')
ax1.set_ylim(0, 0.78)
ax1.set_yticks(np.arange(0, 0.8, 0.1))
ax1.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper left', frameon=False)
ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax1.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax1.set_title('(a) Exec-only ISR*: FOL vs Prolog', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', loc='left', pad=4)

# footnote moved to LaTeX caption for readability

# === Bottom Panel ===
bw2 = bar_w * 1.6
b_h7 = ax2.bar(x, h7, bw2, color=C_TS, label='TS tautological', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)
b_degen = ax2.bar(x, degen, bw2, bottom=h7, color=C_DEGEN, label='Degenerate syntax', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)
b_query = ax2.bar(x, query, bw2, bottom=[h+d for h,d in zip(h7, degen)], color=C_QUERY, label='Query-as-fact', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

ax2.set_xticks(x)
ax2.set_xticklabels(seeds)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate Fig 2: ISR collapse trajectory — ISR reward causes tautological collapse."""

import json
import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ── Okabe-Ito palette (colorblind-safe, consistent with other figures) ──
OI_BLUE = "#0072B2"
OI_RED  = "#D55E00"
OI_SKY  = "#56B4E9"

# ── Style ──
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 11,
    "axes.titlesize": 13, "axes.labelsize": 12,
    "xtick.labelsize": 10, "ytick.labelsize": 10,
    "legend.fontsize": 10, "figure.dpi": 300,
    "savefig.dpi": 300, "savefig.bbox": "tight",
    "savefig.pad_inches": 0.05,
    "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
    "lines.linewidth": 1.8, "pdf.fonttype": 42, "ps.fonttype": 42,
})


def rolling_mean(arr, w=20):
    kernel = np.ones(w) / w
    padded = np.concatenate([np.full(w - 1, arr[0]), arr])
    return np.convolve(padded, kernel, mode="valid")


# ── Load data ──
data_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "fig2_data.json")
with open(data_path) as f:
    data = json.load(f)

W = 20

exec_s44_steps = np.array(data["exec_s44"]["steps"])
exec_s44_smooth = rolling_mean(np.array(data["exec_s44"]["isr"]), W)

isr_s44_steps = np.array(data["isr_s44"]["steps"])
isr_s44_smooth = rolling_mean(np.array(data["isr_s44"]["isr"]), W)

isr_1k_steps = np.array(data["isr_s42_1000"]["steps"])
isr_1k_smooth = rolling_mean(np.array(data["isr_s42_1000"]["isr"]), W)

rand_s44_steps = np.array(data["random_s44"]["steps"])
rand_s44_smooth = rolling_mean(np.array(data["random_s44"]["isr"]), W)

# ── Plot ──
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))

# ISR β=0.1: two seeds showing collapse
ax.plot(isr_s44_steps, isr_s44_smooth, color=OI_RED, linewidth=2.2,
        label=r"ISR $\beta\!=\!0.1$ (seed 44)", zorder=5)
ax.plot(isr_1k_steps, isr_1k_smooth, color=OI_RED, linewidth=1.2,
        alpha=0.5, linestyle="--",
        label=r"ISR $\beta\!=\!0.1$ (seed 42, 1k steps)", zorder=4)

# Exec-only
ax.plot(exec_s44_steps, exec_s44_smooth, color=OI_BLUE, linewidth=2.2,
        label="Exec-only (seed 44)", zorder=5)

# Random β=0.1
ax.plot(rand_s44_steps, rand_s44_smooth, color=OI_SKY, linewidth=2.2,
        label=r"Random $\beta\!=\!0.1$ (seed 44)", zorder=5)

# Annotation: ISR collapse
collapse_step = 280
collapse_isr = isr_s44_smooth[collapse_step - 1]
ax.annotate("ISR collapse\n(Goodhart effect)",
            xy=(collapse_step, collapse_isr),
            xytext=(100, 0.92),
            fontsize=9, color=OI_RED, fontweight="bold",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=OI_RED, lw=1.2),
            ha="center", va="center")

ax.set_xlabel("Training Step")
ax.set_ylabel("ISR (proved samples only, rolling $w$=20)")
ax.set_ylim(-0.02, 1.02)
ax.set_xlim(0, 1050)
ax.legend(loc="center right", framealpha=0.9, edgecolor="none")
ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.3, linewidth=0.5)

# ── Save ──
out_dir = os.path.dirname(__file__)
for ext in ("pdf", "png"):
    out = os.path.join(out_dir, f"fig2_isr_collapse.{ext}")
    fig.savefig(out, format=ext)
    print(f"Saved: {out}")
plt.close()
